title: nixos/sshd: remove 'moduliFile' option, in favour of settings.ModuliFile
reason: Applicable: real sshd module + wired test (nixos/tests/all-tests.nix at head c571adaef contains 'openssh = runTest ./openssh.nix;'). Real diff GENUINELY REMOVES the top-level `moduliFile` mkOption declaration and replaces it with a new `services.openssh.settings.ModuliFile` option inside the settings submodule, wired via a real `lib.mkRenamedOptionModule ["services" "openssh" "moduliFile"] ["services" "openssh" "settings" "ModuliFile"]` -- a genuine option lifecycle (removal+rename) event, flagged by the coordinator in advance as worth examining closely for how oba represents a watched option going from existing to genuinely gone.
targets_toml: single target sshd, cfg_ident=cfg, option_prefix=[services,openssh], watch=[moduliFile] (the OLD path -- deliberately watching the pre-rename location to see how its own disappearance is represented, not the new settings.ModuliFile location).

additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.note: REAL, DISTINCT BASE/HEAD VERDICTS -- exactly the case flagged in advance. At base, moduliFile genuinely existed as a real mkOption (its own value was used as a plain path substitution -- `"ssh/moduli".source = cfg.moduliFile;` -- never as a branch/predicate condition, hence PredicateNotFound, a CORRECT 'exists but no predicate' verdict). At head, moduliFile is genuinely gone (renamed away via lib.mkRenamedOptionModule), so OptionNotFound is also a CORRECT verdict on its own terms. So neither individual verdict is wrong -- the concern is entirely about REPRESENTATION of the base->head TRANSITION, not either endpoint.

MOST IMPORTANT FINDING THIS BATCH, flagging with maximum prominence per the coordinator's explicit instruction: audit-diff's own raw.json DOES correctly detect and classify this transition -- summary.unchanged=0, summary.changed=1, and summary.oba_verdict_transitions = {'predicate_not_found->option_not_found': 1} are all present and correct in the JSON. BUT the rendered, maintainer-facing summary.md table shows ALL-ZERO across every one of its named rows (New findings 0, Resolved findings 0, Findings became inconclusive 0, New inconclusives 0, Resolved inconclusives 0, Removed subjects with a finding 0, Evidence-only changes 0, Unchanged 0) -- there is NO row in the rendered table that this specific verdict-transition class (predicate_not_found->option_not_found) maps onto, so a maintainer reading ONLY summary.md would see a report that looks like nothing happened at all, despite raw.json's own summary.changed field being 1 and a real option-declaration removal having genuinely occurred. Additionally, raw.json's own summary.notable_total=0 and summary.notable=[] -- oba itself does not surface this transition as a 'notable'/actionable presentation candidate either, despite having detected and internally classified it as 'changed'. This is why notable_actionable_presentations above is correctly 0 (nothing was actually PRESENTED to review, by the tool's own current behavior) even though real, detected, structured change data exists in the JSON that a maintainer never sees rendered anywhere. I am not asserting this is a bug or a correctness failure myself -- that determination belongs to the coordinator/reviewer -- but the raw JSON-vs-rendered-summary discrepancy, and the silent non-surfacing of a genuine option-removal transition as 'notable', both seem squarely worth a close look.
